svg.title: Markov Process vs Hidden Markov Process
svg.desc: In a Markov process the state is the data; in a hidden Markov process an observation layer covers it, so the state must be inferred first.
svg.text: Markov Process vs Hidden Markov Process
A chain whose state you see directly vs one where the state hides and only observations show
Count the transitions and you are done
The number of states K and labels
The chain itself is the data
The state hides; only the observation shows
One observation layer laid over the same chain
What we see is this row itself
State X — recorded as it is
Counting transitions is the whole estimation
Normalize the counts by row and you have P
No extra algorithm is needed to estimate it
All we see is the bottom row
Observation y — this is all you get
Working from the bottom row back to the top is state inference
In a Markov process the state is the data; a hidden Markov model lays one observation layer on top.
That one layer forces state inference first, and makes the observation sequence non-Markov.
A hidden Markov model takes a chain
and lays an emission layer on it
The tools for that veil are forward-backward, Viterbi and EM from the sheets that follow.
